title: The Scythe of Elune: The Original Mystery
summary: An Ashenvale inquiry follows Velinde Starsong’s journal across ports to Duskwood. A separate witness account deepens the trail without resolving who next held the Scythe or making every worgen mystery one cause.
opening: At a ruined Ashenvale shrine, a tome preserves a missing priestess’s memory. Her journal carries the search across ports toward Duskwood, where another witness recalls a weapon found and lost. Their separate accounts meet at Roland’s Doom, leaving the Scythe’s next keeper unknown.

chapters.title: The shrine and the journal
chapters.body:
At Forest Song, Melyria spoke of demons pressing out of Felwood and a ruined shrine overtaken by mysterious wolf-men. Their cries had given the hollow its name. She asked the seeker to read the Tome of Mel’Thandris. Amid the forest’s unrest, a sacred ruin and a strange pack held the beginning of a mystery no sentinel could yet explain.

The Tome revealed a memory of Velinde Starsong. As her companions dwindled and her strength failed against the demons, she called to Elune. In the vision, she received the Scythe and believed her prayer answered. Melyria saw more to investigate. A gift had entered the struggle, but the memory had not yet shown what its power would bring into the forest.

Melyria sent the inquiry to Thyn’tel Bladeweaver in Darnassus. Velinde had served at Forest Song before her disappearance. Thyn’tel hesitated to open her belongings to a stranger; the Sentinels still hoped their trusted priestess might return. Between the shrine’s vision and the effects preserved in the city, the search approached a life left unfinished in the memory of her people.

The vision persuaded Thyn’tel to lend the key to Velinde’s chest. Within it lay a journal. Its pages preserved the priestess’s work and doubts, carrying her own understanding of the Scythe. The city had kept those belongings in hope of her return. Now her writing offered a way to follow what she had believed and what had troubled her before she vanished.

Velinde wrote that the Scythe let her speak with the worgen and summon them into her world. The first pack followed her against the demons in Felwood. To the embattled priestess, they offered allies where her own companions had become too few. The wolf-men at Mel’Thandris now stood within a darker question: what else had entered the forest with that desperate hope?

The journal’s later pages darkened. Packs grew when Velinde no longer summoned them, and one sent into the forest never returned. She feared their leaders had passed beyond her control. Leaving the worgen she could gather at the shrine, she sought knowledge in Darnassus and Darkshore. A rumor that Arugal had summoned worgen offered another lead, and she decided to seek the wizard.

chapters.title: A trail of records
chapters.body:
Velinde’s last entry planned a passage from a Barrens port toward the lead concerning Arugal. Thyn’tel sent the seeker to Wharfmaster Dizzywig in Ratchet. The priestess had left an intention rather than an answer. Beyond her final written words, people along the docks might remember where the search had carried her, and whether the hope in those pages had survived the crossing.

At Ratchet, Dizzywig found Velinde’s name beside passage on the Black Osprey to Booty Bay. With no contrary entry, he believed the ship had arrived safely. The ledger offered a named crossing and a likely destination, though no message from Velinde herself. Across the sea, a caravaner might remember what followed her arrival upon the farther shore.

In Booty Bay, Ruzzgot remembered a night elf priestess travelling with his caravan. They parted upon the northbound road, and he recalled her heading toward Darkshire. The search entered Duskwood, where worgen were already feared. From a ship’s ledger to a traveller’s memory, the trail carried Velinde’s absence toward the town whose records might preserve another sign of her passage.

Clerk Daltry found no record of Velinde staying at the inn. Yet he knew of the wolf-men the seeker described and pointed toward the Carevin household. Their hunters opposed the wood’s monsters. Darkshire had yielded no remembered lodging for the missing priestess, but the creatures linked to her search offered another way onward, toward a mine south of the town.

Jonathan Carevin knew the place where worgen had first been found in Duskwood. He asked that Roland’s Doom be searched for a sign of the Scythe. The priestess’s passage remained unconfirmed, and the weapon’s fate unknown. Beneath the forest’s older fears, the mine might hold a trace of the loss that had drawn the search so far from Ashenvale.

chapters.title: Two accounts at Roland’s Doom
chapters.body:
At a mound within Roland’s Doom, Velinde’s specter appeared. She spoke of failure, worgen beyond control and the loss of Elune’s Scythe. Whose hand now directed it, she did not know. The seeker had reached the priestess’s grief, but not the weapon. Beyond her testimony, the moment of her death and the Scythe’s next bearer remained hidden.

Carevin heard what the mine had revealed. He promised to make the worgen’s numbers a priority, though the root of the danger remained beyond his household’s reach. The weapon was still lost. Resistance could be offered where a cure could not. The seeker returned toward Darnassus, carrying Velinde’s grief to those who had kept her belongings in hope.

Thyn’tel received the report as news of Velinde’s fate. A trusted friend had been lost, and the Scythe had passed beyond her people’s keeping. The search ended without recovering it or naming its new bearer. Darnassus could remember the priestess and acknowledge her loss. It could not yet tell where the power she had once welcomed had gone.

Separate testimony survived in a partial book from Sven’s farm, later linked to Jitters. Its writer remembered finding a scythe in Roland’s Doom. Worgen attacked after he pulled it free, and he fled, losing it along the way. He wondered whether his act had brought them, but could not know. Another witness narrowed the mystery to Duskwood without revealing the weapon’s next keeper.

reviewNote: Complete illustrated research story with 15 transcript nodes, nine Classic Scythe quest beats, an independent Sven/Jitters Duskwood witness record, a claim and citation ledger, dedicated Classic-area scenes and cast/object art, and matching narration tracks. All records remain contentStatus research. The two chains are joined editorially, not as quest prerequisites. The story keeps attribution and uncertainty, gives no exact date, route or unproved Duskwood causality, and excludes Gilneas/Cataclysm, later comics, post-Cataclysm area states and the Legion artifact campaign. Original-client quest/item capture, Classic-area/cast comparison, citation/claim review and narration audition remain open. The included Classic accounts do not identify the Scythe’s subsequent bearer; Jitters’s recovered object is not proven to be the same item.
